edits.title: Keep a steady line available for movement
edits.old: Try following it. Then walk alongside it. Cross it at an angle. The stripe gives you something steady to vary your relation with.
edits.new: Try following it. Then walk alongside it. Cross it at an angle. The stripe stays straight through all three journeys.
edits.incitement: The sentence about varying a relation can be made visible: different walks beside a stripe that stays straight.
edits.purpose: Let different movements be compared against a steady geometric mark.
edits.reader_move: Follow, walk alongside and cross the same stripe.
edits.why_here: An unchanging reference makes the difference between the walks available to notice.
edits.without: The invitation ends in an abstract description of a relation.

edits.title: Let the words act without inventing a judge
edits.old: Did a sideways step feel like a mistake? The marking makes no such judgement: its script draws the stripe and lettering without scoring your walk. The instruction may still have changed how you moved.[^point-lines-ahmed-paths] Another visitor might find an invitation to dance around it.
edits.new: Did a sideways step feel like a mistake? The marking does not measure how closely you follow it. Its script draws the stripe and lettering. Yet you may already have corrected a step in answer to the words.[^point-lines-ahmed-paths] You might also find yourself dancing around the same steady line.
edits.incitement: The critical question is in a possible self-correction: words can direct a walk even though the artifact does not assess compliance. Keep dancing available to this reader too.
edits.purpose: Distinguish the effect an instruction may have on a visitor from a programmed score, while retaining playful use.
edits.reader_move: Consider whether the words prompted a correction or another way of moving.
edits.why_here: The reader has just tried several walks and can inspect how the invitation was taken up.
edits.without: The passage risks sounding like a report about absent scoring, with pleasure assigned to another visitor.

edits.title: Meet the line made by moving
edits.old: Turn and look at the route your movement has left behind. Compare it with the stripe. That small sideways step is visible now.[^point-lines-ahmed-deviation]
edits.new: Turn and look at the route your movement has left behind. Compare it with the stripe. Where do the two lines part company?[^point-lines-ahmed-deviation] One was waiting for you; the other has taken shape while you moved.
edits.incitement: Do not promise that every footstep was recorded. Invite comparison between the authored stripe and the line made during movement.
edits.purpose: Make the difference between a prior instruction and a recorded movement available to inspect.
edits.reader_move: Look for where the two lines separate or coincide.
edits.why_here: The trace enters as the consequence of the walk rather than another abstract kind of line.
edits.without: A small step is guaranteed to appear even though the recorder follows the headset and admits samples selectively.

edits.title: Give the recorder a bodily consequence
edits.old: The recorder saves sampled positions and joins them. In VR it follows the headset's horizontal position at the rig's floor height; on desktop it follows the walker. The resulting line records one part of your movement.
edits.new: The recorder saves positions and joins them with straight segments. In VR, the X and Z come from the headset; the line is drawn near floor level. On desktop it follows the walker. A lean can change the drawing even when your feet stay put.
edits.incitement: Following the headset has an approachable consequence: leaning can draw without a step. This teaches what the recorder observes without turning its limitation into a general disclaimer.
edits.purpose: Explain the sampled position and distinguish its trace from a footprint through a movement the reader can try.
edits.reader_move: Consider or try a lean with feet still, then inspect the resulting line.
edits.why_here: After comparing the drawings, identify the moving position from which this one is made.
edits.without: The reader receives a tracking description but little sense of what it changes for the encounter.
